name: Cyclophosphamide
route_note: IV infusion in most chemotherapy regimens; oral tablets/capsules for some cancers and autoimmune disease

discovery.by: Norbert Brock and Herbert Arnold, Asta-Werke
discovery.note: Designed as an inactive 'transport form' of a nitrogen mustard that would be activated preferentially in tumour tissue; activation actually occurs mainly in the liver.

tagline: Prodrug nitrogen mustard used across cancer, transplant and autoimmune medicine
summary: Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating prodrug that is activated by liver cytochrome P450 enzymes into a DNA cross-linking mustard. It is a backbone of many regimens for lymphoma, leukaemia, breast cancer and sarcoma, and is also used as an immunosuppressant in severe autoimmune disease and stem-cell transplant conditioning.
mechanism: Cyclophosphamide itself is inactive. Hepatic CYP2B6 and other P450 enzymes hydroxylate it to 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide, which exists in equilibrium with aldophosphamide and diffuses into cells.

Aldophosphamide breaks down to phosphoramide mustard, the alkylating species that forms interstrand DNA cross-links at guanine N7 positions, blocking replication and triggering apoptosis, and acrolein, a by-product responsible for haemorrhagic cystitis.

Cells rich in aldehyde dehydrogenase (such as haematopoietic stem cells) detoxify aldophosphamide, which partly explains why lymphocytes are depleted while stem cells are relatively spared — the basis of its immunosuppressive and post-transplant uses.
uses: Multiple myeloma, neuroblastoma, ovarian cancer, retinoblastoma and sarcomas
Off-label: lupus nephritis, vasculitis, transplant conditioning and post-transplant GVHD prophylaxis

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Brock and Arnold at Asta-Werke report cyclophosphamide after screening oxazaphosphorine mustards.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves cyclophosphamide (Cytoxan, Mead Johnson) for cancer.

history.title: Activation understood
history.detail: Studies through the 1960s establish that hepatic metabolism is required to generate active metabolites.

history.title: CMF adjuvant trial
history.detail: Bonadonna's CMF trial shows adjuvant chemotherapy benefit in node-positive breast cancer.

history.title: Mesna
history.detail: Mesna is developed to neutralise acrolein and prevent haemorrhagic cystitis with high-dose oxazaphosphorines.

history.title: Post-transplant cyclophosphamide
history.detail: Johns Hopkins investigators popularise high-dose post-transplant cyclophosphamide for haploidentical transplant GVHD prophylaxis.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP3A4 activation; aldehyde dehydrogenase detoxification

facts: Mesna (2-mercaptoethane sulfonate) is co-administered with high doses to protect the bladder from acrolein.
It is one of the most widely used drugs in the WHO list's cytotoxic section.
